subject: physics
question_text: Why are gaps left between the iron rails of a railway track?

mark_split.label: Rails expand in the summer heat
The gap gives room, avoiding buckling

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya IPE Study Material for Jr. Students 2026-27 edition, physics volume, Chapter 11 Very Short Answer Question 5 (printed p.116). Only the question was taken; the answer, its steps and its mark split are original work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. The 1 + 1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Physics hand-checked: iron rails lengthen due to thermal expansion when the temperature rises in summer; a gap left between successive rails gives that expansion room, so the rails do not press against each other and buckle sideways out of alignment.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Rails expand in the heat
lines: In summer the temperature rises and
the iron rails become longer because
steps.margin_note: First mark. Say the rails expand as the temperature rises.
steps.why: A metal rod grows longer when it is heated, and a rail lying in the summer sun over a hot day is no exception.
common_mistakes: Jumping straight to the gap without first saying why the rails expand.

recall.must_convey: That the rails expand and grow longer when the temperature rises in summer.

steps.memory_tip: Heat makes the metal rail grow longer, the same as any heated rod.

steps.label: The gap gives room to expand
lines: Without a gap the expanding rails
would press against each other and
A small gap between successive rails
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Say the gap prevents the rails from buckling.
steps.why: The rail cannot lengthen along the track, so it bends sideways instead; the gap gives the extra length room.
common_mistakes: Saying the gap is for the bolts or joints. The gap is for thermal expansion.

recall.must_convey: That the gap leaves room for the rails to expand, so they do not press against each other and buckle.

steps.memory_tip: The rail cannot lengthen along the track, so it bends sideways instead — the gap gives it room.

insider_note: Two marks — first that the rails expand in the heat, then that the gap gives that expansion somewhere to go instead of buckling the track.
